audit_notes: Parameters positive and within bounds. D = 5e5*(2.5e-4)^3/(12*0.7599) = 8.57e-7 N m; clamped strip under 3 kPa: w_max = p a^4/(384 D) = 0.146 mm (0.58 t, within linear plate theory). Peak edge strain = 16 t w_max/a^2 = 0.146, above the ~0.10 biofilm threshold. Swept volume: mean deflection = (8/15) w_max = 78 um, times a/pitch = 0.8 gives a stroke film of 62 um per unit hull area, 1.7x the groove inventory of 36 um, so one stroke can refill all closed cells; the excess must vent through pores at the cell ends (otherwise the cells overflow and lubricant is lost to the sea; the stroke should be limited by lower pressure or a valve). Concerns: (1) grooves 45 um deep in a 250 um soft skin concentrate strain at the groove roots (stress concentration ~2-3, local strain 30-45 %); silicone tolerates this statically (elongation at break 100-300 %) but fatigue over 1e4 cycles must be tested; (2) soft silicone ridges (E = 0.5 MPa) do not collapse under 50 Pa shear (shear strain ~1e-4), but they abrade far faster than the hard ridges of the parent; (3) 15 % strain widens the grooves temporarily, the meniscus stays pinned if the lubricant wets the groove walls; (4) bladders must be pressure-compensated to hydrostatic pressure. The drag benefit (closed-cell slip ~6 % turbulent plus avoided slime) lies outside the solved deflection field; a static skin has zero stroke and zero strain, so no meaningful relative baseline exists in this field: baseline left empty, gain n/a. Primary metric: stroke film thickness per unit area (integral of w times a/pitch), to be compared with the 36 um groove inventory.
